faqs.question: How do I apply for admission?
faqs.answer: Applications are submitted online through the university admissions portal. Fill out the application form, upload your academic documents, pay the application fee, and submit before the deadline.

faqs.question: What are the admission requirements?
faqs.answer: You need a high school diploma or equivalent, official transcripts, standardized test scores (if required), a personal statement, and letters of recommendation. Specific requirements vary by program.

faqs.question: What is the application deadline?
faqs.answer: The regular decision deadline is January 15 for the fall semester. Early decision applications are due November 1, and spring applications are due October 1.

faqs.question: How much is the tuition fee?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees vary by program and residency status. Domestic undergraduate tuition averages $10,000 per year, while international students pay approximately $25,000 per year.

faqs.question: Can I pay fees in installments?
faqs.answer: Yes, the university offers an installment plan allowing you to split tuition into three payments per semester. Contact the Bursar's Office to enroll.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available?
faqs.answer: Yes, merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. Submit the scholarship application along with your admission application by the priority deadline of December 1.

faqs.question: How do I access my timetable?
faqs.answer: Log in to the student portal and go to Academics > My Timetable. You can view your weekly schedule, room locations, and instructor names there.

faqs.question: Can I change my timetable?
faqs.answer: You can add or drop courses during the add/drop period, which is the first two weeks of the semester. Use the student portal or speak with your academic advisor.

faqs.question: When are the final exams?
faqs.answer: Final exams are held during the last two weeks of each semester. The exam schedule is published four weeks before the exam period on the student portal.

faqs.question: What if I miss an exam?
faqs.answer: Contact your instructor immediately. Makeup exams are granted only for documented emergencies or medical reasons, and must be approved by the department head.

faqs.question: Where is the library located?
faqs.answer: The main library is in the Central Campus Building, Floor 3. Branch libraries are located in the Science Wing and the Arts Complex.

faqs.question: What are the library opening hours?
faqs.answer: The main library is open Monday–Friday 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM, and Sunday 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Hours may vary during holidays and exam weeks.

faqs.question: How do I borrow a book?
faqs.answer: Use your student ID card at the circulation desk or the self-checkout kiosks. Undergraduates may borrow up to 10 books for 28 days.

faqs.question: Can I reserve a study room?
faqs.answer: Yes, study rooms can be reserved online through the library website or at the library services desk. Reservations are available in 2-hour blocks.

faqs.question: How do I join a student society?
faqs.answer: Browse societies at the annual Societies Fair or on the student union website. Click 'Join' on any society's page, or attend their next meeting as a guest.

faqs.question: How do I start a new society?
faqs.answer: Gather at least 10 interested students, draft a constitution, and submit a proposal to the Student Union for approval. Approved societies receive funding and meeting space.

faqs.question: Where can I find contact information?
faqs.answer: Visit the Contact Us page on the university website. Key offices: Admissions (admissions@university.edu), Registrar (registrar@university.edu), and IT Helpdesk (it@university.edu).

faqs.question: What is the university phone number?
faqs.answer: The main switchboard is +1 (555) 123-4567. Admissions: ext. 201, Registrar: ext. 202, Library: ext. 203, IT Helpdesk: ext. 204.

faqs.question: What is the university email address?
faqs.answer: General inquiries: info@university.edu. Admissions: admissions@university.edu. Registrar: registrar@university.edu. IT support: it@university.edu.

faqs.question: Where is the university located?
faqs.answer: The university is located at 123 Campus Drive, College City, State 54321, USA. The campus is a 15-minute drive from the city center.

faqs.question: How do I reset my student portal password?
faqs.answer: Click 'Forgot Password' on the student portal login page, enter your student email, and follow the reset link sent to your inbox. Alternatively, contact the IT Helpdesk.

faqs.question: How do I get a student ID card?
faqs.answer: New students receive their ID card at orientation. Replacement cards cost $15 and can be issued at the Campus Card Office in the Student Center.

faqs.question: Is on-campus housing available?
faqs.answer: Yes, on-campus housing is available in several residence halls. Apply through the Housing Portal by June 1 for the fall semester. Rooms are assigned on a first-come, first-served basis.

faqs.question: What meal plans are available?
faqs.answer: Three meal plans are offered: 19 meals/week, 14 meals/week, and 10 meals/week, all with dining dollars. Purchase or change plans through the Housing Portal.

faqs.question: Is there a health center on campus?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Student Health Center is in the Wellness Building and offers medical consultations, mental health counseling, and pharmacy services. Open Monday–Friday 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

faqs.question: How do I get a transcript?
faqs.answer: Request official transcripts through the student portal under Academics > Transcripts. The first copy is free; additional copies cost $5 each.

faqs.question: Who is my academic advisor?
faqs.answer: Your academic advisor is assigned based on your major. Find your advisor's name and contact details in the student portal under Academics > My Advisor.

faqs.question: Can I transfer credits from another university?
faqs.answer: Yes, credits from accredited institutions may be transferred. Submit your official transcript and course syllabi to the Registrar's Office for evaluation.

faqs.question: Is there a career services office?
faqs.answer: Yes, Career Services is in the Student Center and offers resume reviews, mock interviews, job listings, and career counseling. Book an appointment online.

faqs.question: How do I report a technical issue?
faqs.answer: Contact the IT Helpdesk at it@university.edu or ext. 204, or submit a ticket at support.university.edu. Include your student ID and a description of the issue.
